blurb: macOS uses code signing, notarisation, Gatekeeper, runtime protections, and malware detection to help users run trusted software while preserving the flexibility of the Mac. In macOS 26.4, Terminal paste protection warns less-experienced users before commands copied from common attack-vector apps are executed, while XProtect can inspect activity resulting from pasted terminal commands and block known malicious sources or behaviour. AppleScript scanning adds another layer against scripts commonly used in social-engineering campaigns.
